_comment: Shared truth table for the community-report phone normalizer, which is implemented
reporter), JavaScript (worker/community-reports-worker.js, the public HTTP trust
boundary), and Python (scripts/phone_normalization.py, issue-filed reports and bulk
imports). All three must land a given report on the SAME database key or the row can
Every implementation's test suite loads this file and asserts its own column, so a fix
applied to one language and not the others fails the build. This exists because the
national-trunk-prefix fix (issue #6, c4cf98f) landed in Kotlin and Python but not in
the worker, leaving the public endpoint able to store unmatchable rows for months.
A null expectation means the implementation must REJECT the input. The Kotlin column
is null for bare national numbers by design: the app always has an E.164 number from
PhoneNumberUtils, so a missing '+' there means the input is untrustworthy. The other
two accept hand-typed reports and apply the 10-digit -> NANP heuristic.

cases.why: China: national trunk 0 typed into the international form. Issue #6 - the reported number.
Same number already in E.164 - normalization must be idempotent.
UK: the (0) notation is the trunk prefix and is not part of the E.164 number.
Germany: trunk 0 before the Berlin area code.
Australia: trunk 0 before the area code.
Italy KEEPS its leading 0 - it is part of the national significant number, not a trunk prefix. Stripping it would corrupt a valid Rome number.
Cote d'Ivoire KEEPS its leading 0 after the 2021 ARTCI renumbering (01/05/07 mobile, 21/25/27 fixed).
NANP has no trunk prefix; the one-digit country code must split correctly.
Russia: the other one-digit country code.
Singapore: two-digit code, no trunk prefix, total length 10 - must not be NANP-ified.
Denmark: explicit international 10-digit total. The bare-10-digit NANP heuristic must never apply to a +-prefixed number (v1.7.27 fix).
Bare national. Kotlin rejects (the app always holds E.164); the hand-typed report paths apply the NANP heuristic. Intentional divergence.
Bidi/zero-width marks pasted from a chat client, wrapping a trunk-prefixed number.
All-zero national part: leave the digits alone rather than strip to nothing, and let the length/plausibility gates reject it.
Arabic-Indic digits are not ASCII digits - all three must reject rather than silently drop them.
16 digits exceeds the E.164 maximum of 15.
